title: dark-factory project profile
description: Contents of .factory/profile.json in a consumer project. The profile only adds project-specific values to the factory core; it cannot remove or override anything the core ships. Every element is off unless the profile enables it.

$schema.description: Optional reference to this schema, for editor support.

branchTemplate.description: Branch name template for task branches. Placeholders: {issue} (issue number) and {slug} (title slug), for example "task/ISSUE-{issue}-{slug}".

githubProject.description: Optional number of the GitHub Project the project issues are tracked in.

install.description: Project-level dependency installation steps, run in a fresh clone once and in order before the installation steps of any app. Same command contract as apps[].install (argv array, no shell; cwd relative to the project root). Optional; absent or empty means no steps and nothing is added implicitly. The token {file} is a literal here, never substituted.

dependencySync.description: Dependency synchronization after the Ralph agent changed the root manifest. Optional; absent means no command. The core decides when it runs: a git status entry (either side of a rename, deletions included) with the path package.json in the root. The root manifest is served by this root area and by an app with path ".". Commands run after the last agent pass and before the final gate, once per affected area (root first, then apps in profile order, commands in array order), in the sandbox with the install specification: read-only .git, the run network with the proxy, the validated sandbox.installEnv; never on the host. Ordinary install, apps[].install and setup are not repeated. A changed manifest whose serving areas have no command, a package.json outside the root and the app paths, or a failing, timed-out or sandbox-failed command makes the issue BLOCKED before the final gate, commit, push and PR. The core does not parse the package manager's argv and never substitutes npm. The commands must not run lifecycle scripts of the project or its dependencies (for npm: npm install --ignore-scripts). {file} is a literal here.

apps.description: Application layout of the project. A single-package project lists one app with path "."; a monorepo lists one app per package.

name.description: Short app name, unique within the profile.

path.description: App directory relative to the project root; "." for a package in the root.

install.description: Dependency installation steps run in a fresh clone, in order. Optional; no steps by default.

gate.description: Gate commands run for this app before a commit, in order. Optional; no gate by default. The Ralph agent and both reviewers are allowed exactly these commands: for each one the argv joined with single spaces, and the same followed by " *" for extra arguments.

dependencySync.description: Dependency synchronization after the Ralph agent changed exactly <path>/package.json of this app (for an app with path ".": the root package.json). Optional; absent means no command. Same execution and BLOCKED rules as the root dependencySync; the commands must not run lifecycle scripts (for npm: npm install --ignore-scripts).

docOnlyPathPatterns.description: Glob patterns (minimatch: *, **, {a,b}; dot true, matchBase false, nonegate true, nocomment true; profile/path-patterns.js) of paths whose changes are documentation only. Paths are relative to the project root, \ is normalized to /. *.md covers the root only, **/*.md any depth; an entry ending with / stands for all its content (X/ is X/**). Matching is case-sensitive. A diff is doc-only only when every changed path matches, both sides of a rename and deleted and binary files included; an empty or absent list means no diff is doc-only. A pattern is never a string prefix.

protectedPaths.description: Glob patterns of paths the Ralph agent must not change, with the syntax of docOnlyPathPatterns (an entry ending with / stands for all its content). Matching ignores letter case on every platform, and X/ also protects the path X itself (a file or link in place of the directory). The controller checks every entry of git status --porcelain -z -uall after each agent turn: new untracked files one by one, changes, deletions, both sides of a rename or copy, type changes and binary files by path regardless of content; .git/ is also checked by a fingerprint. The core always protects .git/ and .claude/ in addition. Edit/Write deny rules derived from these entries may be wider than the pattern, never narrower; the controller check decides.

labels.description: GitHub label names used by the factory.

humanNeeded.description: Label that marks an issue or PR as needing a human.

calibration.description: Label that, set by an owner on an issue or its PR, asks Calibration Judge to analyse a failed verifier round. Required when judge.enabled is true.

verifier.description: Acceptance Verifier settings. The verdict itself is computed by code; these values only locate inputs and name the result.

verdictCheckName.description: Name of the status check that carries the verifier verdict.

goldenDir.description: Directory of reference cases (inputs with an expected verdict), relative to the project root. The golden eval reads its cases only from here; without it the eval fails instead of using a default.

checks.description: Names of the deterministic verifier checks that run for this project (core checks: spec-approval, affects-scope, computed-items, test-tampering-scan, references, ci-checks, allowed-model). Checks not listed stay off; none run by default. A name no registered check has fails the verdict.

skillRules.description: Project entries of the shared "path to skills" table. They are added to the core table and cannot remove or override its entries.

path.description: Path prefix, relative to the project root, that the entry applies to.

extensions.description: File extensions that the entry applies to, each with the leading dot. Plain (".ts") and compound (".test.ts", ".d.ts") extensions are accepted; every segment after a dot is non-empty and contains no whitespace, "/" or backslash. An extension is matched as a suffix of the file name.

label.description: Human-readable label of the entry, shown in hook messages.

skills.description: Names of skills that must be loaded before editing matching files.

extraMetaskills.description: Names of metaskills installed in the project in addition to the base set of the package.

ruleFiles.description: Project rule files (for example a CLAUDE.md) that agents must read, relative to the project root.

overlays.description: Project overlays of document templates, relative to .factory/overlays/. An overlay can only add to a core template.

prd.description: Overlay file for the PRD template.

plan.description: Overlay file for the plan template.

issue.description: Overlay file for the issue template.

docs.description: Locations of project documents, relative to the project root.

adr.description: Path of the one file with architecture decision records, relative to the project root (a file, not a directory). The ADR rule of the shared path-to-skills table applies to exactly this file, matched exactly after path separators are normalized. Without it no ADR rule is added and the adr skill reports that no ADR file is configured.

hooks.description: Commands of the lint and typecheck hooks. A hook is inactive for paths that no entry matches. The event of a hook is bound to a changed file; the entry command may check that one file (pass it with the {file} token) or the whole project (omit the token).

lint.description: Lint commands per path. On a changed file the hook runs every entry whose paths match the file (at least one pattern matches), in array order, each entry once however many of its patterns match. A failing or missing binary of one command is recorded in diagnostics and does not stop the following ones; the lint hook itself always exits 0. {file} in command.argv is substituted as described in hookCommand.

typecheck.description: Typecheck commands per path. Selection and execution are the same as for hooks.lint: every entry that matches the changed file, in array order, once each; a failure of one command is recorded in diagnostics and does not stop the following ones; the typecheck hook always exits 0. {file} in command.argv is substituted as described in hookCommand.

agentEnvironment.description: Environment constraints stated to the Ralph agent in its prompt (for example tools that are unavailable). The sandbox section is added by a later schema revision.

judge.description: Calibration Judge, the optional observer that analyses failed Acceptance Verifier rounds. Off unless "enabled" is true; a disabled Judge needs no other fields. Judge only observes: it never changes a verdict, a status or a label.

enabled.description: Whether Judge runs in this project, in any way of starting it. Absent or false means off. When true, labels.calibration is required.

sandbox.description: Docker sandbox of the Ralph runtime: the image and the pinned tool versions, the egress allowlist and the install environment. Required when ralph.enabled is true; when given it is always validated, whether Ralph is enabled or not. The semantic rules (explicit image tag, exact claudeCodeVersion, host names, reserved variable names) are those of ralph/sandbox.js validateSandboxConfig, applied by loadProfile. Holds no credentials. The runs root is not a profile setting: it belongs to the consumer's local run config outside Git.

image.description: Docker image reference with an explicit tag (name:tag) that the runtime builds and runs.

nodeVersion.description: Node.js version of the image, numeric: 22, 22.1 or 22.1.2.

claudeCodeVersion.description: Exact version X.Y.Z of the claude CLI installed in the image; no range, tag or pre-release.

allowedHosts.description: Host names the egress proxy lets the sandbox reach (CONNECT to port 443, exact name only): DNS names of at least two labels, no scheme, IP, port, path or wildcard.

installEnv.description: Optional environment for dependency installs inside the sandbox: string values, names matching ^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*$. Proxy, DOCKER_*, GIT_*, GCM_*, GH_*, HOME and CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR are reserved. Absent means {} (normalized by the runtime only).

ralph.description: Ralph, the autonomous issue-executing agent. Off unless "enabled" is true; a disabled Ralph needs no other fields.

enabled.description: Whether Ralph runs in this project. When false, no other ralph field is required.

techDebtTrackerIssue.description: Number of the issue that collects tech-debt items. Required when Ralph is enabled.

humanNeededVerdict.description: Name of the verdict with which the Ralph agent reports that a human decision is needed (for example BLOCKED-<REASON>). Optional; absent means none is configured and nothing is assumed. A non-empty string without whitespace (a trailing newline included) and without a colon; it must not be a service token (DONE, BLOCKED, TYPE, SUMMARY, REVIEW, CODEREVIEW). Regex characters are allowed and are interpreted literally by the reader. It is not the label labels.humanNeeded and not the verifier status check verifier.verdictCheckName.

enabledSteps.description: The complete Ralph step pipeline of this project, in run order. Absent means the baseline pipeline: implement, self-review, code-review, final-gate. An explicit list is the whole pipeline: "implement" is mandatory and first, "final-gate" is mandatory and last (each exactly once); "self-review" and "code-review" may be left out, and when both are listed "self-review" comes first; other registered steps go between them and run only when listed here. An empty list is invalid (it has no mandatory step). Names are checked against the step registry before the run starts.

stepBudgets.description: Fix budget per review step: step name -> integer >= 1, the number of fix calls after a fixable review failure (a budget of 4 allows at most five review calls). A step not named keeps its default (self-review and code-review: 2). Budgets are independent; the task's time and cost limits still apply. A key must name a registered step with a fix; a budget of a registered step that is not in enabledSteps is allowed and does not enable it.

command.description: A command as an argument array (not a shell string) plus its working directory. The strings are passed as they are: the token {file} is substituted only inside hooks.lint[].command.argv and hooks.typecheck[].command.argv (see hookCommand); in install, gate and dependencySync commands it is a plain literal.

cwd.description: Working directory relative to the project root; "." for the root.

hookCommand.description: A hook command bound to the paths it applies to. paths are glob expressions with minimatch semantics (*, ** and {a,b}), relative to the project root and written with "/"; the changed file path is made relative with "/" before matching. ** matches zero or more directories, so **/*.ts also matches x.ts in the root. Options: dot true, nocase false, matchBase false, nonegate true, nocomment true; braces and globstar stay enabled. A file outside the project root matches no entry. In command.argv the optional token {file} is replaced, in every occurrence in every string element (also inside a longer element such as --file={file}), by the absolute path of the changed file inside the project root, the same for any cwd. The result stays one argument: no shell, no extra quoting, no interpretation of path characters. cwd and other fields are not interpolated. Without the token the command runs with its arguments unchanged.

paths.description: Glob patterns of the paths the command applies to.
